memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Follow my decrees and be careful to obey my laws, and you will live
safely in the land. Then the land will yield its fruit, and you will eat
your fill and live there in safety'" - Lev 25:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God connects obedience with security here. As Israel followed His ways,
they would dwell safely and eat their fill in the land.

We must read this carefully and in its proper place. This was a specific
covenant promise to the nation of Israel about a specific land. It was not
a formula that guarantees every obedient believer material comfort. Godly
people in Scripture suffered hunger, exile and loss, and Jesus Himself had
nowhere to lay His head. We must never twist this into a
health-and-wealth promise.

But we can draw the timeless principle beneath it, because God's character
does not change. Living God's way genuinely does bring a security the
world cannot offer — not always outward ease, but a deep-rooted stability
of soul.

Dear reader, Jesus said the wise man who hears His words and puts them into
practice is like a house built on rock; when storms came, it did not fall
(Matt 7:24-25). Notice the storms still came. The security was not the
absence of storms but the presence of a foundation.

Paul, in prison, could speak of a peace that transcends understanding,
guarding his heart (Phil 4:7). That is the safety God offers His people
now — not a life without trouble, but a soul that cannot be shaken.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I seeking outward comfort or the unshakable security God offers?
2. Where am I building my life on something other than Christ?
3. Have I confused God's peace with the absence of problems?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for a security that does not depend on my circumstances.
Build my life on Christ, so that whatever storms come, I will not be
shaken. Amen.
